# Vendored crates

## gpui-pre-macos 0.3.11

An unmodified copy of the `gpui-pre-macos` 0.3.11 registry release (Apache-2.0, see `gpui-pre-macos/LICENSE-APACHE`), wired in through `[patch.crates-io]` in `client/Cargo.toml`, with one SQLLY patch: when the build environment sets `SQLLY_APP_STORE=1` (the Mac App Store build script does), its `build.rs` enables `cfg(sqlly_app_store)`, which compiles out the private AppKit selectors that App Review rejects under guideline 2.5.1 — the `_opaqueRectForWindowMoveWhenInTitlebar` and `_windowRestorationOptions` overrides, the `_zoomFill:` window action (public `zoom:` is used instead) and the private diagonal-resize `NSCursor` methods (the public macOS 15 frame-resize cursors, or a crosshair, are used instead). Every patched spot is marked `SQLLY patch` in `src/window.rs`. Without `SQLLY_APP_STORE=1` the crate behaves exactly like the registry release.

A second `SQLLY patch` (also in `src/window.rs`, where each window picks its frame source) paces frames with the crate's `CVDisplayLink` registry instead of `CAMetalDisplayLink`. With the 0.3.11 Metal display link, a window sometimes skipped the repaint after an edit: typed text was in the buffer but stayed invisible until the next resize or activation. That happened on a macOS 26 VM; gpui 0.3.9 and the `CVDisplayLink` path never did it. Setting `SQLLY_METAL_DISPLAY_LINK=1` restores the upstream choice. Re-test it before dropping the patch on a later bump.

When bumping `gpui-pre`, re-copy the matching `gpui-pre-macos` release from the registry, re-apply the `SQLLY patch` hunks and `build.rs`, and run `build-app-store.sh`, whose private-API scan fails the build if any private selector slips back in.

## tiberius 0.13.0

An unmodified copy of the `tiberius` 0.13.0 registry release (MIT OR Apache-2.0, see `tiberius/LICENSE-MIT.txt` and `tiberius/LICENSE-APACHE.txt`), wired in through `[patch.crates-io]` in `client/Cargo.toml`, with one opt-in SQLLY patch: the registry release decodes SQL Server's INFO tokens (`PRINT`, `RAISERROR` with severity 10 or lower) and DONE-family row counts but never hands either to callers, so the SQL Server Messages pane could show neither. The patch adds `QueryItem::Info(TokenInfo)` and `QueryItem::Done(DoneInfo)` (with `DoneKind`), the `QueryStream::with_info_messages()` / `with_done_tokens()` flags, and `Client::simple_query_with_server_messages()`, which sets both flags before the stream advances to its first item so messages ahead of the first result set are kept. `forward_to_metadata` stops at an opted-in token, `into_results` / `into_row_stream` / `into_row` and the `as_*` / `into_*` accessors skip the new items, `TokenInfo` gets public accessors (`message`, `number`, `class`, `state`, `line`, `procedure`, `server`) and is exported from `lib.rs` with `DoneInfo` and `DoneKind`, and `TokenDone` gets crate-private `counted_rows` / `has_more` / `is_error` / `command` helpers. Every patched spot is marked `SQLLY patch` in `src/lib.rs`, `src/client.rs`, `src/tds/stream/query.rs`, `src/tds/codec/token/token_info.rs` and `src/tds/codec/token/token_done.rs`; unit tests for the new items are at the end of `src/tds/stream/query.rs`. Streams built without the flags (`query`, `simple_query`, `execute`) behave exactly like the registry release. The copy keeps the crate's own `.gitignore`, which leaves its `Cargo.lock` untracked.

The vendored crate is not a workspace member, so `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo clippy --workspace` do not touch it and `cargo test -p tiberius` refuses to run it (it has dev-dependencies). To run its tests, copy the folder outside `client/` and run `cargo test --lib --no-default-features --features tds73,rustls,chrono` there. When bumping `tiberius`, re-copy the new release from the registry, re-apply the `SQLLY patch` hunks (`diff -r` against the registry copy shows them), and drop the patch if upstream has started surfacing INFO and DONE tokens itself.
